subject: NeonTech productization & feedback license routing
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neontech.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dan.kim@neontech.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Productization rights & feedback license — draft redlines

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — the NeonTech product team is excited about embedding Redwood for our in-app assistant. Our legal team attached a first-pass redline of the MSA + Order Form (NeonTech_Redlines_v1.docx). Primary asks:

- Output ownership: we need explicit language that NeonTech owns customer-facing outputs (generated content) for productization and downstream commercial use.
- Training/data use: NeonTech cannot have derivative use of our data for any model retraining or product improvements without explicit opt-in.
- Feedback license: we can provide telemetry signals and non-PHI feedback, but only under an anonymized, aggregated license and after a 30-day buffer; no attribution.

Could you confirm which of these are acceptable under Redwood standard terms and where we should expect to see alternative options (pay-for opt-out / dedicated deployments)? We prefer to resolve IP and training carveouts during the order form step rather than escalating into a long legal review.

Appreciate a quick sketch of options so we can share internally.

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Sr. Counsel, NeonTech
legal@neontech.com

Attachment: NeonTech_Redlines_v1.docx (redline of MSA + Order Form)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neontech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Productization rights & feedback license — draft redlines

Hi Olivia — thank you and the NeonTech team for the clear markup and the priorities. Quick responses below, and looping in Jordan (legal) and Laura (sales lead) to propose concrete language and options.

1) Output ownership: Our standard approach is that customers have rights to use and commercialize outputs they receive from the service. We can accept contractual language that clarifies NeonTech may productize outputs generated by your end-users. We usually carve out the right for Redwood to retain aggregated telemetry for service analytics.

2) Training / model retraining: Redwood does not, by default, train public models on customer data. We offer an explicit opt-in for customer data to be used in model retraining (paid add-on). Otherwise, we limit training to internal synthetic datasets and public corpora.

3) Feedback license: We can accept an anonymized, aggregated feedback license with a short buffer. Jordan and I discussed three practical options:
  - Standard: Redwood may use de-identified telemetry and aggregated feedback for service improvement (no customer-identifiable content).
  - Opt-out (paid): NeonTech pays a premium for a Training Opt-Out addendum that prohibits use of signals for model improvements.
  - Private deployment: Dedicated/Private deployment where all telemetry remains in your VPC (higher price / longer lead time).

I'll let Jordan propose succinct MSA language and Laura will follow with the pricing/ops implications. Suggest a 30-min call next week to go over the three paths and agree which to put in the order form.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Productization rights & feedback license — draft redlines

Hi Olivia — Jordan here (legal). Thanks for the redline — reviewed and annotated. High-level legal position and a proposed set of replaceable clauses:

- Customer Output: We can agree a clause that grants NeonTech a broad, perpetual, worldwide license to use and commercialize outputs generated for your customers. Redwood will include language that prevents assignment of Redwood proprietary components (i.e., we won't transfer model weights or internal IP).

- Feedback / Telemetry: Proposed language: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide, perpetual license to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and feedback solely to improve and operate Redwood services, provided such use is non-attributable to Customer and subject to a 30-day data buffering period." This preserves operation/improvement while addressing attribution concerns.

- Training / Retraining: We will add explicit opt-in language: "Redwood will not use Customer-provided data to train or update models used in the service unless Customer explicitly opts in via a separate Training Addendum, which includes pricing and scope of data use."

- Escrow / Evidence: If NeonTech requires auditability, we can offer redacted telemetry reports and limited sampling for compliance review under NDA.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We prepare a single tracked-change MSA response (RNW_NeonTech_Response_redline.docx) with the above language and mark the alternative commercial options inline.
2) Laura to propose the pricing delta for Opt-Out and Private deployment and add a short clause for the Order Form that selects the option.

If these positions look reasonable, I'll circulate the redline today. Otherwise call out any absolute deal-breakers.

—Jordan Blake
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia — Laura here. Following Jordan's legal markup, we've prepared a response package and a short commercial matrix to make choices explicit for the Order Form. Attached: RNW_NeonTech_Response_redline.docx and Pricing_matrix_feedback_options.csv. Summary of the path forward:

Option A (Standard):
- Customer owns outputs for productization.
- Redwood retains right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for service improvements (30-day buffer).
- No model retraining on Customer data without opt-in.
- Implementation: standard hosted plan; no price change.

Option B (Training Opt-Out — Paid):
- Same customer output language; Redwood contractually agrees not to use telemetry or signals for model improvement.
- Pricing: +15% ARR premium (covers masking, data segregation, and accounting).

Option C (Private/Dedicated):
- Dedicated deployment with telemetry kept in your VPC; contractual prohibition on Redwood using any telemetry for model training.
- Pricing and lead time: separate SOW; estimated procurement timeline 8–12 weeks.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which option NeonTech prefers or flag any absolute redline changes by EOD Thur (July 1).
2) If you want Option B or C, we will include the specific addendum language in the Order Form and circulate the updated quote.
3) We can do a 30-min call Wed (June 30) 10–10:30 PT to walk through the matrix — Sean will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Renewals & Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
